name: STAK Energy Campus Gas Pipeline

values.EndLocation: STAK Energy Campus, Dalton Highway milepost 390
values.DataCenterNotes: The pipeline would feed the gas-fired power plant of the STAK Energy data center campus, a computing facility of up to 3 gigawatts.

researcher_notes: STAK Energy Corp has applied to the Alaska Division of Oil and Gas for a 50-year state land lease for a gas-powered computing campus of 1 to 3 gigawatts at Dalton Highway milepost 390, about 26 road miles south of Deadhorse. The application, as described by Petroleum News in June 2026, includes associated gas pipeline infrastructure connecting to existing or developing North Slope gas fields 25 to 90 miles from the site, and the division has made a preliminary decision to approve the lease. A DatacenterDynamics article from May 2026 also says the campus would be fed by new gas pipelines. This now meets the data center add-threshold: a named sponsor, a named project in Alaska, and a public filing that names the project. Route, length, diameter, start point, gas supplier and pipe owner are not named, so those cells stay blank and the route is marked no route. Petroleum News estimates fuel use at 350 to 500 million cubic feet per day; that is a demand estimate, not a stated pipe capacity, so capacity is left blank. Owner is the lease applicant; the pipe may end up held by another company. The owner name was checked against the ownership team's style and has no existing entity match. This is not an existing row: nearby North Slope rows are TAPS-area or long-haul lines. An earlier run classed this as monitor under the old endpoint rule. The two sources are not fully independent of the same lease filing. Confidence is low.
